title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

reports.title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

summary:
Rebecca Green agreed to let an AI scribe transcribe her first urologist appointment, but it invented a claim that she microdosed psychedelic mushrooms. She found the false statement in a post-operative letter after kidney stone surgery in March and feared it could harm her workers' compensation case. After she complained, the urologist apologized, corrected the record, and said she would review how AI was used in her practice. AHPRA reminded clinicians they must check all AI output.

A Digital Rights Watch report found unregulated AI scribes can record wrong details, such as the wrong breast in a cancer diagnosis or a false epilepsy history. The Royal Australian College of GPs estimates 40 per cent of GPs regularly use AI scribes. The Therapeutic Goods Administration is reviewing these tools and will release findings in coming weeks, with breaches to be acted upon. The advocacy group wants an approved list of tested AI scribes. Ms Green says she would only consent again with a doctor she already knows.
